## Details

### `GET /api/admin/admins`

Helper admins and the list of grantable privileges.

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  admins: [{ adminId, login, privileges, authorized }],
  allPrivileges: ['queue_manage', '…'],
}
```

Password hashes are never included. `allPrivileges` is convenient for building the permission form.

### `POST /api/admin/admins`

Creates a helper admin.

**Request body:**

```js
{ login: '…', password: '…', privileges: ['queue_manage'] }
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, admin: { … }, message: { uk: '…', en: '…' } }
```

The password here is **temporary**: the account starts with `authorized: false` and can do nothing until the helper activates it through `/admins/self/activate`.

### `DELETE /api/admin/admins/:id`

Deletes a helper admin.

If they are online, their connection receives `force_logout` with `reason: "admin_deleted"` and the session ends at once.

### `PUT /api/admin/admins/:id/privileges`

Changes a helper admin's permissions.

**Request body:**

```js
{ privileges: ['queue_manage', 'stats'] }
```

If the helper is online they immediately receive a `privileges_updated` event — the change applies **without logging in again**.

### `PUT /api/admin/admins/:id/reset-password`

Resets a helper admin's password to a new temporary one.

**Request body:**

```js
{ newPassword: '…' }
```

The account becomes unauthorized again and must be re-activated.

### `POST /api/admin/admins/self/activate`

A helper admin activates their own account.

**Request body:**

```js
{ tempPassword: '…', newPassword: '…' }
```

**Errors:** `400` — not applicable to the super admin, or the temporary password is wrong

The only action available to a helper with `authorized: false`. On success an `admin_authorized` event follows.

### `PUT /api/admin/admins/self/login`

Changes your own login name.

**Request body:**

```js
{ newLogin: '…', currentPassword: '…' }
```

**Errors:** `400` — not applicable to the super admin, or the password is wrong

### `PUT /api/admin/admins/self/password`

Changes your own password.

**Request body:**

```js
{ currentPassword: '…', newPassword: '…' }
```

**Errors:** `400` — not applicable to the super admin, or the password is wrong

The super admin's password can only be changed via `ADMIN_PASS` in `.env`.

### `GET /api/admin/artist-arts`

Artists, flagged by whether artwork exists.

Records are created automatically when a daytime track is uploaded.

### `DELETE /api/admin/artist-arts/:artist`

Deletes an artist's artwork.

The artist record itself remains; only the image goes away.

### `GET /api/admin/artist-arts/file/:artist`

The artwork file for preview in an admin UI.

Unlike the client-facing `/api/artist-art/:artist`, it is served unwrapped.

### `POST /api/admin/artist-arts/upload`

Uploads an artist image.

**Headers:** `Content-Type: image/jpeg`

**Request body:**

```js
raw JPEG bytes, up to 10 MB
```

**JPEG only** — PNG or WebP are rejected. The image is expected to be already cropped to a portrait format: the client does that before sending.

### `GET /api/admin/audit`

The admin action log.

**Query:** `window` — `24h` and other spans; `limit` (default 30); `offset`

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, entries: [ … ], total, offset, limit }
```

Served from an in-memory cache, so the query is cheap. Entries are purged automatically after `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` days. No special privilege — every admin may read it.

### `GET /api/admin/background-music`

Background tracks, paginated.

A host on air sees the same list through the `host_get_background_music_list` event.

### `GET /api/admin/background-music/:id/audio`

Background track audio for previewing.

Works exactly like `/api/admin/jingles/:id/audio`: a presigned link in the cloud, a link to `/api/admin/background-music/file` locally.

### `POST /api/admin/background-music/:id/used`

Enables or disables a track in the selection pool.

### `POST /api/admin/background-music/batch-delete`

Deletes several background tracks.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…'] }
```

### `POST /api/admin/background-music/batch-move`

Moves background tracks between modes.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…'], targetMode: 'day' | 'night' }
```

### `GET /api/admin/background-music/counts`

How many background tracks are available.

Open to any admin, like the jingle counter.

### `GET /api/admin/background-music/file`

Serves the background music file itself from local storage.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night`; `filename` — the file name; `adminToken` — the admin token

The direct counterpart of `/api/admin/jingles/file`: only needed on local storage, and accepts the token in the header or the query string.

### `POST /api/admin/background-music/upload`

Uploads a background track.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night`

**Headers:** `X-File-Name`, `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`

**Request body:**

```js
raw MP3 bytes, up to 80 MB
```

On success a `background_music_updated` event follows.

### `POST /api/admin/background-music/upload-check-duplicate`

Checks the filename before uploading.

**Request body:**

```js
{ filename: 'ambient.mp3' }
```

### `GET /api/admin/donations/history`

Donation history, filterable by time window.

**Query:** `window` — `24h` \| `7d` \| `30d` \| `max` (all, bounded by `DONATION_RETENTION_DAYS`); `limit`, `offset` — pagination

**Response:**

```js
{ entries: [{ id, uid, songId, songTitle, songArtist, provider, currency, amount, tier, status, createdAt, paidAt }], total, offset, limit }
```

Requires `donations_manage`.

### `GET /api/admin/donations/price-preview`

First-tier price for an arbitrary duration — for the settings modal preview.

**Query:** `durationSeconds` — optional, defaults to the longest track in the library

**Response:**

```js
{ basePrice: 1 }
```

Requires `donations_manage`. Computes against the already-saved settings, not unsaved form values.

### `GET /api/admin/donations/settings`

Current donation settings and the active provider.

**Response:**

```js
{
  settings: {
    currency: 'UAH', pricingMode: 'fixed' | 'calculated',
    fixedPrice: 1, pricePerSecond: 0.02,
    tiersEnabled: true, tierCeiling: 5,
    blockDonationsWhileChatting: false,
  },
  radioHostsMode: false,
  provider: null | { id: 'donatello', displayName: 'Donatello', supportedCurrencies: ['UAH'] },
  historyCurrencies: ['UAH'],   // валюти, що реально зустрічались в історії донатів
  donationRetentionDays: 365,
}
```

Available to any admin without a dedicated privilege — same pattern as `GET /api/admin/settings`. Writing requires `donations_manage`.

### `POST /api/admin/donations/settings`

Saves donation settings.

**Request body:**

```js
{ currency, pricingMode, fixedPrice, pricePerSecond, tiersEnabled, tierCeiling, blockDonationsWhileChatting }
```

**Response:**

```js
{ settings: { … }, clamped: false }
```

If `tiersEnabled` and the worst case (the longest track in the library for `calculated`, or `fixedPrice` for `fixed`) at the top tier exceeds the provider’s max transaction amount, `tierCeiling` is automatically lowered and the response is flagged `clamped: true`.

### `GET /api/admin/history`

The full playback history.

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, entries: [ … ], total }
```

Requires the `stats` privilege. Entries are purged automatically after `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` days — the same schedule as the admin action log.

### `GET /api/admin/jingles`

Jingles, paginated and searchable.

Served from an in-memory cache, so the query is cheap.

### `GET /api/admin/jingles/:id/audio`

Jingle audio for previewing in an admin UI.

Returns `{ url }`. In the cloud that is a presigned link straight to the bucket; on local storage it is an absolute link to `/api/admin/jingles/file` carrying the token as a query parameter.

### `POST /api/admin/jingles/:id/used`

Enables or disables a jingle in rotation.

A disabled jingle stays in storage but never goes on air — handy for parking a seasonal jingle without deleting it.

### `POST /api/admin/jingles/batch-delete`

Deletes several jingles at once.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…', '…'] }
```

### `POST /api/admin/jingles/batch-move`

Moves several jingles between day and night mode.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…'], targetMode: 'day' | 'night' }
```

Files are moved in storage, so the operation is not instant.

### `GET /api/admin/jingles/counts`

How many jingles exist and how many are usable on air.

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  day: 12, night: 8,              // total
  dayUsable: 10, nightUsable: 6,  // marked as active
  minRequired: 3,                 // minimum needed for rotation
}
```

The only endpoint in this section that does not need `jingles_uploader`, so any admin can see the state. If fewer than `minRequired` are usable, jingles are not inserted into the broadcast.

### `GET /api/admin/jingles/file`

Serves the jingle file itself from local storage.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night`; `filename` — the file name; `adminToken` — the admin token

Only needed on local storage: in the cloud the client follows a presigned link to the bucket instead. The token is accepted in the header or in the query string, because the waveform player fetches the URL with a plain `fetch` and no headers. Escaping the jingles directory gives `400`, a missing file `404`.

### `POST /api/admin/jingles/upload`

Uploads a jingle.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night` (default `day`)

**Headers:** `X-File-Name`, `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`

**Request body:**

```js
raw MP3 bytes, not multipart. Limit: 80 MB
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, jingle: { id, filename, mode, duration, used } }
```

**Errors:** `400` — empty body, not an MP3, or the configuration does not support jingles; `409` — that filename already exists

As with track uploads, the body is raw bytes. A new jingle is active right away (`used: true`). If the database write fails the file is removed from storage, so no orphans are left behind. On success a `jingles_updated` event is broadcast.

### `POST /api/admin/jingles/upload-check-duplicate`

Checks whether a jingle with that filename already exists.

**Request body:**

```js
{ filename: 'jingle.mp3' }
```

Jingle filenames are unique globally, not per mode.

### `POST /api/admin/login`

Admin login.

**Request body:**

```js
{ login: '…', password: '…' }
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true }              // in production
{ ok: true, token: '…' }  // in development
```

**Errors:** `400` — login or password missing; `401` — wrong credentials

**In production the token is not in the response body** — it arrives only in the httpOnly `adminToken` cookie. Your client must send requests with `credentials: "include"`, and its origin must be listed in `CLIENT_ORIGIN`. The token lasts 12 hours. Login attempts are rate-limited.

### `POST /api/admin/logout`

Logout: clears the token cookie.

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true }
```

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/audio-preview`

A URL for audio playback while aligning timings in the editor.

**Query:** `title` and `artist`

**Response:**

```js
{ url: 'https://…' }
```

In cloud mode a temporary R2 URL; in local mode a URL to `/api/audio/stream/admin`, which accepts the admin token and needs no art/audio tokens.

### `DELETE /api/admin/lyrics/cache`

Removes lyrics from the cache.

**Query:** `title` and `artist`

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, existed: true }
```

After deletion the lyrics are fetched from LRCLIB again on next access.

### `PUT /api/admin/lyrics/cache`

Saves edited lyrics.

**Request body:**

```js
{ title: '…', artist: '…', entry: { synced: true, lines: [{ time, text }] } }
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true }
```

Keyed by the artist + title pair, not by track identifier.

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/cache-entry`

Lyrics for a single track.

**Query:** `songId`, or the `title` + `artist` pair

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/cache-full`

The complete lyrics cache.

Returns everything in one go — a heavy response for a large library.

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/cache-index`

A lightweight index of which tracks already have lyrics.

**Response:**

```js
{ items: [ … ] }
```

Cheaper than `/cache-full` when you only need the list.

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/offsets`

All stored lyrics timing offsets.

### `GET /api/admin/lyrics/songs`

Tracks with their lyrics status — the editor's input data.

**Response:**

```js
{ items: [ … ] }
```

### `GET /api/admin/phrases`

Phrases, paginated and searchable.

Served from an in-memory cache, so the query is cheap.

### `GET /api/admin/phrases/:id/audio`

Phrase audio for previewing in an admin UI.

Returns `{ url }`. In the cloud that is a presigned link straight to the bucket; on local storage it is an absolute link to `/api/admin/phrases/file` carrying the token as a query parameter.

### `POST /api/admin/phrases/:id/used`

Enables or disables a phrase in rotation.

### `POST /api/admin/phrases/batch-delete`

Deletes several phrases at once.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…', '…'] }
```

### `POST /api/admin/phrases/batch-move`

Moves several phrases between day and night mode.

**Request body:**

```js
{ ids: ['…'], targetMode: 'day' | 'night' }
```

Files are moved in storage, so the operation is not instant.

### `GET /api/admin/phrases/counts`

How many phrases exist and how many are usable on air.

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  day: 5, night: 3,               // total
  dayUsable: 4, nightUsable: 2,   // marked as active
  minRequired: 1,                 // minimum needed to enable "Phrases on air"
}
```

The only endpoint in this section that does not need `jingles_uploader`, so any admin can see the state. Unlike jingles, the "Phrases on air" setting in the admin panel stays disabled (not just warned) until every active mode has at least `minRequired` usable phrases.

### `GET /api/admin/phrases/file`

Serves the phrase file itself from local storage.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night`; `filename` — the file name; `adminToken` — the admin token

The direct counterpart of `/api/admin/jingles/file`: only needed on local storage, and accepts the token in the header or the query string.

### `POST /api/admin/phrases/upload`

Uploads a phrase.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night` (default `day`)

**Headers:** `X-File-Name`, `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`

**Request body:**

```js
raw MP3 bytes, not multipart. Limit: 10 MB
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, phrase: { id, filename, mode, duration, used } }
```

**Errors:** `400` — empty body, not an MP3, longer than ~5 seconds, duration could not be determined, or the configuration does not support phrases; `409` — that filename already exists

Unlike jingles and background music, duration is strictly enforced here: a phrase longer than 5 seconds (with a small tolerance), or one whose duration could not be read at all, is rejected outright. A new phrase is active right away (`used: true`). If the database write fails the file is removed from storage. On success a `phrases_updated` event is broadcast.

### `POST /api/admin/phrases/upload-check-duplicate`

Checks whether a phrase with that filename already exists.

**Request body:**

```js
{ filename: 'phrase.mp3' }
```

Phrase filenames are unique globally, not per mode.

### `GET /api/admin/settings`

All radio settings.

Available to any admin without a special privilege — the interface needs this data to initialise. Only writing is restricted.

### `POST /api/admin/settings`

Saves settings; each section under its own privilege.

**Request body:**

```js
{
  branding:   { telegram_url, byLang: { uk: { dayRadioName, … } } },
  generation: { DAY_ALGORYTM, MAX_DAY_DURATION, GROUP_DEFS, … },
  radioHosts: { guestMaxDurationMinutes, specialGuestMaxDurationMinutes, backgroundMusicMode },
  songGroups: [ … ],   // ignored
}
```

**Errors:** `403` — missing the privilege for a section that changes; `400` — validation failed

Authorization is based on what **actually changes**, not on what was sent: the admin panel always posts every section. `branding` needs `settings_branding`, `generation` needs `settings_algorithm`, `radioHosts` needs `radio_moderator`. `songGroups` is ignored here: groups are edited through `/api/admin/song-groups`. See [Privileges](/en/reference/privileges).

### `DELETE /api/admin/song-editor`

Deletes a track from the library and from storage.

**Errors:** `409` — the track is playing now or is up next

Requires `editor_meta`. If it was the artist's last daytime track, their artwork record is removed too. Non-super-admins have a daily deletion quota.

### `POST /api/admin/song-editor/batch-delete`

Deletes several selected tracks.

Requires `editor_meta`. Locked tracks are skipped rather than failing the whole operation. The daily quota is 30 deletions for non-super-admins; the response reports the remainder when exceeded.

### `POST /api/admin/song-editor/batch-move`

Moves several tracks between modes.

Requires `editor_meta`. Works on any storage.

### `GET /api/admin/song-editor/download`

Downloads the track's source file.

Requires `editor_meta`. Serves the same MP3 that sits in storage.

### `POST /api/admin/song-editor/move-mode`

Moves a track between day and night mode.

Requires `editor_meta`. The file is physically moved between modes - between bucket prefixes or between folders on disk, depending on the storage. The track identifier changes with the mode, since it contains the mode.

### `POST /api/admin/song-editor/save`

Saves metadata, lyrics and lyrics offset for a track.

**Request body:**

```js
{
  songId: 'day/artist - title.mp3',
  metadata: { title, artist, album, year },
  metadataChanged: false,   // the flags decide which privileges are required
  lyricsEntry: { … },  lyricsChanged: false,
  offset: 0,           offsetChanged: false,
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — `songId` or `metadata` missing; `403` — missing the privilege for what is being changed; `404` — track not found; `409` — the track is locked

Which privilege is needed depends on the flags: editing metadata requires `editor_meta`, editing lyrics requires `editor_lyrics` or `editor_meta`. **`409` is an expected answer**, not a failure: a track cannot be edited while it is playing or up next, and the reason arrives in the `localized` field. Changing metadata rewrites the ID3 tags in storage, so the track identifier may change.

### `GET /api/admin/song-groups`

All song groups with track counts and a preview.

**Response:**

```js
{ items: [{ id, name, mode, songCount, songsPreview }] }
```

Any admin may read; changing them requires `settings_groups`.

### `POST /api/admin/song-groups`

Creates a song group.

**Request body:**

```js
{ name: '…', mode: 'day' | 'night', songs: ['day/…'] }
```

Requires `settings_groups`.

### `DELETE /api/admin/song-groups/:groupId`

Deletes a song group.

Requires `settings_groups`. Tracks already queued are unaffected.

### `PUT /api/admin/song-groups/:groupId`

Updates a group: its name or its tracks.

**Request body:**

```js
the same fields as on creation
```

Requires `settings_groups`.

### `POST /api/admin/song-groups/:groupId/insert`

Queues an entire group.

**Errors:** `400` — the group is empty, does not fit before the mode switch, or a cooldown applies

Requires **both** `queue_manage` and `settings_groups`, because the action touches both the broadcast and the group definitions. Holding only one is not enough. The `admin_insert_song_group` event does the same thing with the same requirements, so the rule cannot be bypassed over the socket.

### `GET /api/admin/song-groups/library`

Searches the library to populate a group.

**Query:** `mode` (default `day`), `query`, `offset` (0), `limit` (5)

### `GET /api/admin/songs`

The whole library for a mode, with lyrics status.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night`; without it, the radio's current mode

**Response:**

```js
[{
  id: 'day/artist - title.mp3',
  title: 'Title', artist: 'Artist',
  filename: 'day/artist - title.mp3',
  lyricsStatus: 'synced' | 'plain' | 'none',
}]
```

Unlike the public `/api/library`, this lets you pick either mode and adds lyrics state. No special privilege is needed beyond being an authenticated admin.

### `GET /api/admin/stats`

Aggregate statistics for the library and the broadcast.

**Response:**

```js
an object summarising modes, groups and durations
```

Requires the `stats` privilege. Computed on the fly from engine state.

### `POST /api/admin/switch-mode`

Switches the radio between day and night mode.

**Request body:**

```js
{
  targetMode: 'day' | 'night',
  scheduledTime: '23:30',   // optional, HH:MM in the server's time zone
}
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true }
```

**Errors:** `400` — `targetMode` is not `day`/`night`, or the time is not `HH:MM`; `409` — switching now is not allowed (a cooldown applies, or a donated track is queued)

Without `scheduledTime` the switch happens immediately. A time that has already passed today is treated as tomorrow. On `409` the response carries a `donated` flag explaining the reason.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-batch-delete`

Deletes just-uploaded tracks.

Requires `upload_songs`. Meant for undoing a fresh upload, whereas `song-editor/batch-delete` works on the whole library and needs a different privilege.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-batch-move`

Moves just-uploaded tracks between modes.

Requires `upload_songs`.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-check-duplicate`

Checks whether a track already exists, before uploading the file.

**Request body:**

```js
{ trackId: 'day/artist - title.mp3' }
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, exists: false }
```

A cheap check ahead of a long upload. `trackId` is built as `<mode>/<filename>`.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-song-commit`

Upload step 3: puts the track into the library.

**Request body:**

```js
{
  metadata: { … },      // from step 1, possibly edited by the user
  lyricsEntry: { … },   // from step 2, optional
}
```

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, track: { … }, lyricsStatus, lyricsFormat, lyricsMessage, message }
```

**Errors:** `400` — `metadata.filename` or `metadata.mode` missing, or the write failed

Until this step the track takes no part in the broadcast. On success the server broadcasts a `library_updated` event — refresh your lists from it. For daytime tracks an artist artwork record is created as well.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-song-file`

Upload step 1: stores the MP3 and reads its tags.

**Query:** `mode` — `day` or `night` (default `day`)

**Headers:** `X-File-Name` — percent-encoded filename; `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`

**Request body:**

```js
raw MP3 bytes, not multipart. Limit: 80 MB
```

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  storageKey: 'day/artist - title.mp3',
  metadata: { artist, title, album, year, duration, mode, filename, storageKey },
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — empty body or not an MP3; `409` — a track with that filename exists; `400` — storage write failed

The body is sent as raw bytes (`express.raw`), **not** as `multipart/form-data` — that is the most common cause of a `400` here. Metadata is read from ID3 tags, with fallbacks for missing fields. The track does not enter the library yet.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-song-lyrics`

Upload step 2: looks the lyrics up through LRCLIB.

**Request body:**

```js
{ title, artist, album?, duration? }
```

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  lyricsEntry: { synced: true, lines: [{ time, text }] },
  lyricsStatus: 'synced' | 'plain' | 'none',
  lyricsFormat: '…',
  message: { uk: '…', en: '…' },
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — `title` or `artist` missing; `500` — LRCLIB could not be reached

This step is optional and needs no credentials at all: LRCLIB is open. Even on `500` the response contains a usable `lyricsEntry` with `notFound: true`, so the upload can continue.

### `POST /api/admin/upload-song-url`

Downloads audio from YouTube into storage.

**Request body:**

```js
{ url: 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…' }
```

The longest operation in the whole API: it includes downloading and re-encoding through FFmpeg. The track then goes through the same lyrics and commit steps as a normal file upload.

### `GET /api/admin/verify`

Validates the session and returns current privileges.

**Response:**

```js
{
  ok: true,
  role: 'super_admin' | 'admin',
  adminId: '…', login: '…',
  privileges: ['queue_manage', '…'],
  authorized: true,
}
```

**Errors:** `401` — invalid session, or the account no longer exists

For helper admins privileges are re-read from the database rather than taken from the token — which is why permission changes take effect without logging in again. Call this when your admin UI starts.

### `POST /api/admin/youtube-cookies`

Stores YouTube cookies for age-restricted videos.

**Request body:**

```js
{ cookies: '… # Netscape HTTP Cookie File …' }
```

**Errors:** `400` — empty, or the string does not contain `youtube.com`

Cookies are written to the server's temp directory and live until restart. They are only needed for restricted videos. This is sensitive data: it grants access to the account it came from.

### `POST /api/admin/youtube-track-info`

Reads the track list behind a video or playlist URL.

**Request body:**

```js
{ url: 'https://www.youtube.com/…', lang: 'uk' }
```

**Errors:** `400` — URL missing or not a YouTube link; `503` — the tool is unavailable; `504` — reading the playlist took too long

Downloads nothing — it only reports what the URL contains so the user can choose.

### `GET /api/admin/ytbdown-status`

Whether the YouTube download tool is ready.

**Response:**

```js
{ ok: true, … }
```

Call this before showing the import form: the tool needs Python and FFmpeg and is unavailable on some deployments.

### `GET /api/art/url`

A URL for artist artwork instead of the bytes.

**Query:** `artist` — the artist name

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` / `?token=`

**Response:**

```js
{ url: 'https://…', ttl: 900 }
```

In `cloud` mode this is a temporary R2 URL and the image is **not** wrapped. In `local` mode it points back at `/api/artist-art/:artist`, so the response still has to be decoded.

### `GET /api/artist-art/:artist`

Artist artwork.

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` / `?token=`

**Response:**

```js
XOR-wrapped image bytes; the real MIME type is in the `X-Art-Mime` header
```

**Errors:** `400` — invalid name; `404` — no artwork

The `X-Art-Mime` header is exposed via `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, so browsers can read it. Artist names are normalized to lower case.

### `GET /api/audio-key`

Exchanges an art token for a short-lived audio token.

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` and `X-Listener-Uid` — both required

**Response:**

```js
{ token: '<audioToken>', expiresIn: 900 }
```

**Errors:** `400` — `X-Listener-Uid` missing; `401` — art token invalid or expired

The response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. Refresh early — the reference client does so 30 seconds before expiry.

### `GET /api/audio/stream`

Audio bytes for the current or a requested track.

**Query:** `track` — the identifier from `sync` or `/api/library`

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` + `X-Audio-Token`, or the same values as `artToken` and `audioToken` in the query

**Errors:** `400` — `track` missing; `401` — invalid tokens; `404` — track not found

In `local` mode it serves bytes with HTTP Range support. In `cloud` mode it answers `302` redirecting to a temporary R2 URL — allow redirects if you fetch manually. Audio is **not** XOR-encrypted: the tokens are only a pass. For `<audio src>` the tokens have to go in the query, since headers cannot be set there.

### `GET /api/audio/stream/admin`

Track audio for admin interfaces.

**Query:** `track` — the track identifier

Accepts the admin token in a header **or in the query**, and needs no art/audio tokens. That is what makes it usable for `<audio src>` in the editor, where headers cannot be set.

### `GET /api/audio/url`

A URL for the audio, without serving the bytes.

**Query:** `track` — the track identifier

**Headers:** same as `/api/audio/stream`

**Response:**

```js
{ url: 'https://…', ttl: 900 }   // ttl in cloud mode only
```

Useful when your player wants the URL up front. In `local` mode it returns a URL back to `/api/audio/stream` with the tokens already embedded.

### `GET /api/avatar/:filename`

A listener avatar.

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` / `?token=`

**Response:**

```js
XOR-wrapped image bytes; MIME type in `X-Art-Mime`
```

**Errors:** `400` — invalid filename; `404` — file not found

The filename arrives in the `usersUpdate` event, in the `img` field.

### `GET /api/history`

The last 10 played songs.

**Response:**

```js
[{ id, trackId, title, artist, album, mode: 'day' | 'night', playedAt }]
```

No tokens needed. Not affected by the current mode (day/night) — just the most recently played tracks in chronological order.

### `GET /api/library`

Tracks available to request in the current mode.

**Response:**

```js
[{ id: 'day/artist - title.mp3', title: 'Title', artist: 'Artist' }]
```

No tokens needed. Returns only tracks of the current mode (day or night), sorted by artist. The `id` is what you send in `suggest_song`.

### `GET /api/lyrics`

Time-synced lyrics for a song.

**Query:** `title` and `artist` are required, `album` is optional

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` / `?token=`

**Response:**

```js
// after XOR decoding — JSON:
{
  synced: true,
  lines: [{ time: 32.5, text: 'a line' }],
  offset: 0,        // timing correction for this track
  notFound: false,  // true when no lyrics were found
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — `title` or `artist` missing; `500` — `fetch_failed`

The response body is **XOR-wrapped** with the key from the art token, and `Content-Type` is `application/octet-stream`. Decode first, then `JSON.parse`. If the lyrics are not cached, the server tries LRCLIB — that request is noticeably slower.

### `POST /api/lyrics/offset`

Stores the lyrics timing offset for a track.

**Request body:**

```js
{ title: '…', artist: '…', offset: 0.5 }
```

**Errors:** `400` — `title` or `artist` missing

Note the path: it has **no** `/admin` prefix even though it requires an admin token. The offset is in seconds and may be negative.

### `GET /api/public/config`

How the server is configured. The only endpoint with no authentication at all.

**Response:**

```js
{
  dataProvider:   'json' | 'sql',
  musicSource:    'local' | 'cloud',
  nightMode:      true,     // whether a night mode exists at all
  streamMode:     false,    // false = sync mode, true = shared MP3 stream
  radioHostsMode: false,    // whether live broadcasting is possible
  allPrivileges:  ['queue_manage', '…'],
  timeZone:       'Europe/Kyiv',
  capabilities:   { uploadTracks: true, editSettings: true, … },
}
```

Every client starts here: `streamMode` decides how you obtain audio, and `musicSource` tells you whether to expect a redirect to cloud storage. `capabilities` toggles individual features on/off based on server configuration (storage, data provider); `donationInfo` is `null` when `capabilities.donations` is off, otherwise it is the active donation configuration, useful for showing pricing/tiers before ever calling `/donations/tiers`.

### `GET /api/public/donations/:id/status`

Current status of a specific donation.

**Response:**

```js
{
  status: 'pending' | 'paid' | 'paid_unqueued' | 'failed' | 'expired',
  tier: 2 | null,
  matchCode: 'F7BQFF' | null,
  expiresAt: 1700000000000 | null,
}
```

**Errors:** `404` — no donation with that `id`, or it belongs to a different `uid`

Ownership is checked against the `uid` derived from the request IP — the same one the donation was stamped with on creation. Meant for the payment return page (`checkout`) or for polling while waiting on a code (`matching`).

### `POST /api/public/donations/create`

Places a donation order for a song at the chosen tier.

**Request body:**

```js
{ songId: 'day/artist - title.mp3', tier?: 2 }
```

**Response:**

```js
// flowType: 'checkout' (LiqPay, Stripe)
{ donationId: '…', flowType: 'checkout', redirectUrl: 'https://…' }

// flowType: 'matching' (Donatello, Ko-fi)
{
  donationId: '…', flowType: 'matching',
  pageUrl: 'https://…', matchCode: 'F7BQFF',
  amount: 40, currency: 'UAH', expiresAt: 1700000000000,
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — donations are disabled or the chosen tier is unavailable; `404` — song not in the library; `409` — the song is currently playing, up next, or donations are paused (`RADIO_HOSTS_MODE`)

The song is queued **only** after server-side payment confirmation (a webhook for `checkout`/Ko-fi, polling for Donatello) — never directly from the client. For `matching` providers no `redirectUrl` is returned: show `pageUrl` and ask the donor to include `matchCode` in their donation comment; the outcome arrives via the `donation_result` event or by polling `/donations/:id/status`.

### `GET /api/public/donations/tiers`

Computed donation-tier prices for a specific song.

**Query:** `songId` — required, the `id` from `/api/library`

**Response:**

```js
{
  currency: 'UAH',
  pricingMode: 'fixed' | 'calculated',
  tiersEnabled: true,
  tiers: [{ tier: 1, price: 1 }, { tier: 2, price: 2 }, …],  // подвоюється з кожним tier
  flowType: 'checkout' | 'matching',
  chattingBlocked: false,
}
```

**Errors:** `400` — donations are disabled; `404` — song not in the library; `409` — the song is currently playing or up next

`tiers` is an empty array when even the first tier exceeds the active provider’s max transaction amount. `flowType` tells you what to expect from `POST /donations/create`: `checkout` returns a `redirectUrl` right away, `matching` returns the creator’s page and a confirmation code instead. `chattingBlocked` only applies under `RADIO_HOSTS_MODE` — the queue is paused and donations are temporarily refused.

### `GET /api/stream`

The shared MP3 radio stream (stream mode only).

**Headers:** `X-Art-Token` / `?token=`

**Errors:** `404` — the server runs in sync mode; `503` — the stream is not ready yet

An endless response: the client just plays it as a stream. Position for the UI comes from the `stream_get_seek` and `stream_ping` events. Sending `Icy-MetaData: 1` turns on ICY metadata (`icy-metaint` + in-band `StreamTitle`) for external players like VLC or foobar2000.

### `GET /api/stream/public.mp3`

The same stream without a token — a permanent link for external players.

**Errors:** `404` — the server runs in sync mode; `503` — the stream is not ready yet

No authorization at all — deliberately a separate path from `/api/stream`, which stays token-gated for the site’s own web client. Paste this link into VLC, a car radio, or any Shoutcast/Icecast-compatible player once and forget about it. The `.mp3` extension in the path is deliberate: some players (VLC, foobar2000, Winamp) pick which module opens a URL based on its extension, and without one they may treat it as a plain file instead of a live ICY stream. The response sends the full `icy-*` header set (`icy-name`, `icy-genre`, `icy-br`, `Server: Icecast`) unconditionally, without waiting for `Icy-MetaData: 1` - that lets the player recognize it as Icecast-compatible and reconnect on its own to request the embedded metadata (`icy-metaint` + in-band `StreamTitle`). The body is a raw, unbounded stream with no `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (`Connection: close`), matching real Icecast/Shoutcast - a player's ICY parser counts bytes directly in the response body, and HTTP chunk framing throws that count off.

### `POST /webhooks/donations/:provider`

Payment confirmation from a donation provider.

**Response:**

```js
`200` always (even on rejection) — so providers do not retry needlessly; `404` — unknown/unconfigured provider
```

Not meant to be called from a client. `:provider` is one of `liqpay`, `stripe`, `donatello`, `kofi`. Mounted **before** `express.json()`, so the signature is verified against the raw request body: HMAC for LiqPay/Stripe, a `verification_token` for Ko-fi. Donatello never posts here — it is polled instead of receiving a webhook.
